title: ATLAS: Dual-Horizon Diagnostic Evaluation for Industrial Tool-Use Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.30685v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in user-facing services that require iterative tool use under dynamic business conditions. Reliable evaluation is essential for sustained improvement: it must reveal capability deficiencies, inform priorities, and assess interventions. Yet industrial agent service unfolds both through the iterative trajectory of a current request and through continued user interaction. Final-outcome assessment can therefore obscure where deficiencies arise and whether later service remains aligned with context from earlier exchanges. We propose ATLAS, a dual-horizon diagnostic evaluation framework for industrial tool-use agents. At the request horizon, trajectory-wise diagnostic signals relate deficiencies to execution locations and capability concerns. translated_title: ATLAS：面向工业工具使用智能体的双视野诊断评估框架
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体正日益被部署于面向用户的服务中，这类服务需要在动态业务条件下进行迭代式工具调用。可靠的评估对持续改进至关重要：它必须能够揭示能力缺陷、指导优先级排序并评估干预措施的效果。然而，工业级智能体服务既通过当前请求的迭代轨迹展开，也通过用户与系统的持续交互展开。因此，仅评估最终结果可能会掩盖缺陷产生的具体位置，以及后续服务是否仍与早期交流的上下文保持一致。我们提出了ATLAS，一个面向工业工具使用智能体的双视野诊断评估框架。在请求视野层面，基于轨迹的诊断信号将缺陷与执行位置及能力问题相关联；在交互视野层面，基于用户的信号评估服务在持续交互过程中是否保持响应性。两者结合，这些视角为……
tldr: ATLAS提出了一个双视野诊断评估框架，通过请求层面的轨迹级诊断信号（定位缺陷的执行位置与能力问题）和交互层面的用户级信号（评估持续交互中的服务响应一致性），对工业工具使用智能体进行全面的诊断式评估。
en_tdlr: ATLAS is a dual-horizon diagnostic evaluation framework for industrial tool-use agents that combines trajectory-wise diagnostic signals at the request horizon to localize deficiencies with user-wise signals at the interaction horizon to assess service responsiveness across continued interaction.
